ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Preventive Visit — Martin Luther

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Professor Luther comes for a preventive visit. The stone passed nine days after his sick visit and he brought it in; it has gone for analysis. He stopped naproxen after a week and tamsulosin when the stone passed. He has had one short vertigo attack, of about two hours, ten days ago, with the left ear roaring, and used meclizine once. He has kept salt down at home but eats salted meats when he dines out. He has taken sertraline 50 mg for three weeks, with loose stools for a few days at first; his mood is a little better and he is sleeping somewhat better. He has no thoughts of harming himself. He has started weekly therapy. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-09-08; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

Recurrent attacks of spinning vertigo for about three months, the worst twelve days ago, lasting hours, with roaring tinnitus, fullness and muffled hearing in the left ear and nausea, the tinnitus persisting between attacks; with low mood, poor sleep and loss of interest; cause not established at intake: an inner-ear disorder suspected, with vestibular migraine, vestibular schwannoma and posterior circulation stroke to be excluded and depression to be assessed; otology consultation requested
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented attacks of April and July 1527; superseded by the diagnoses at the second visit.

Ménière disease of the left ear, definite (AAO-HNS 2020 and Bárány Society criteria), with low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and persistent tinnitus in the left ear; vestibular migraine considered and judged unlikely as the main cause; vestibular schwannoma excluded by MRI
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the otology consultation, linked to his documented attacks and to the retrospective diagnosis of Ménière disease (R).

Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate (DSM-5-TR), with low mood, poor sleep, loss of interest, guilt and fatigue for about two months, after earlier periods of spiritual crisis and low mood; no suicidal ideation
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to his documented Anfechtungen and low periods; not a claim that he was so diagnosed; the retrospective psychiatric readings are disputed (R).
Urinary stone disease: one stone passed spontaneously last year after severe pain; stone type and metabolic risk not yet known at intake
S — Synthetic modern problem anchored to his documented first stone in 1526.

Right distal ureteral stone, 5 mm, at the ureterovesical junction, with mild right hydronephrosis and renal colic; no infection; kidney function normal; managed with naproxen and tamsulosin; passed nine days later; resolved
S — Synthetic acute problem anchored to his documented recurrent stones; this episode is not a historical claim.

Periodic adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the prevention plan made. Tdap and influenza vaccine given. Lipids today: total cholesterol 214, triglycerides 168, HDL 41 and calculated LDL 139 mg/dL; with no diabetes, normal blood pressure and no smoking, his estimated ten-year cardiovascular risk is low, so a statin is not indicated, and diet, activity and weight are the plan. Hemoglobin A1c 5.6 percent: no prediabetes. HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B screening ordered. Colorectal screening due at 45. [S]
Hepatitis B vaccination to start once the screening result is back.
Walk 30 minutes on most days; aim for 5 percent weight loss.
Lipids again in about five years.
Next preventive visit in one year.

Ménière disease of the left ear (H81.02). One shorter attack in four weeks on the thiazide and salt limit. [S]
Continue; the six-week review will check sodium and potassium.

Recurrent depression (F33.1). PHQ-9 12, from 15, three weeks into sertraline 50 mg and therapy; no suicidal ideation. [S]
Safety plan reviewed and unchanged; 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number confirmed.
Continue sertraline 50 mg and weekly therapy.

Urinary stone disease (Z87.442). The stone has passed and is at the laboratory. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 16 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent, recorded in the chart and not named here, and wants full treatment in any illness from which he could recover. He wants his faith and his pastor's visits respected in any serious illness. The plan will be revisited in a year or sooner if his health changes. [S]
